'''Nathan Mantel''' (February 16, 1919 – May 25, 2002)<ref>{{cite news |author1=Anahad O'Connor |author-link1=Anahad O'Connor |title=Nathan Mantel, 83, Developer Of Statistical Research Method |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/06/08/us/nathan-mantel-83-developer-of-statistical-research-method.html |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150527204138/https://www.nytimes.com/2002/06/08/us/nathan-mantel-83-developer-of-statistical-research-method.html |archive-date=27 May 2015 |access-date=20 July 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=8 June 2002 |page=B 8}}</ref> was an American [[biostatistician]] best known for his work with [[William Haenszel]] that led to the [[Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel statistics|Mantel–Haenszel test]] and its associated estimate, the Mantel–Haenszel [[odds ratio]]. The Mantel–Haenszel procedure and its extensions allow data from several sources or groups to be combined while avoiding [[confounding]].<ref>{{Citation
 | last1 = Mantel| first1 = N.
 | last2 = Haenszel|  first2 = W.
 | year = 1959
 | title = Statistical aspects of the analysis of data from the retrospective analysis of disease
 | journal = Journal of the National Cancer Institute
 | volume = 22
 | pages = 719–748
 | pmid = 13655060
 | issue = 4
 | postscript = .
 | doi=10.1093/jnci/22.4.719
}}</ref>

He spent much of his career working for the [[National Cancer Institute]]. During his career, he published over 380 academic papers. Later in his life, Mantel was known for defending the [[tobacco industry]] against claims that [[passive smoking]] was harmful.<ref>{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Woods |title='Passive Smoking' Report is Disputed |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |date=July 18, 1981 |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1129&dat=19810718&id=joNIAAAAIBAJ&pg=6763,3133468 }}</ref>
